item.title: OpenAI backers question $852B valuation amid strategy shifts
item.description:
Some of OpenAI's own backers are questioning whether the company's $852 billion valuation can hold up as it pivots toward the enterprise market and contends with mounting competitive pressure from Anthropic and Google, according to a report by the Financial Times on Tuesday.

The concerns come just weeks after OpenAI closed a $122 billion funding round — the largest in Silicon Valley history — led by Amazon, Nvidia, and SoftBank, with additional backing from Andreessen Horowitz, Abu Dhabi's MGX, and T. Rowe Price. Yet some investors told the Financial Times the company has redrawn its product roadmap twice in the past six months in response to competitive threats, first from Google and then from Anthropic, raising questions about strategic coherence ahead of a potential initial public offering later this year.

item.title: BP expects 'exceptional' Q1 trading results from war-driven oil volatility
item.description: BP said on Tuesday it expects its oil trading desk to deliver "exceptional" first-quarter results, as the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran sent crude prices surging and created the kind of volatile market conditions in which the company's traders thrive.

item.title: China lifts restrictions on some BHP iron ore purchases
item.description:
China's state-backed iron ore buyer has told several steel mills they may resume purchasing some BHP cargoes, marking a thaw in a months-long commercial dispute that has roiled global iron ore markets. BHP shares rose on Tuesday following the news, reported first by Bloomberg.

Officials from China Mineral Resources Group told plants they can resume bidding for some BHP cargoes denominated in U.S. dollars starting Tuesday, according to Bloomberg, citing people familiar with the matter. Mills have not yet been explicitly allowed to take physical deliveries from Chinese ports, but a notice is expected. Reuters separately confirmed that China has lifted bans on procurement of the steelmaking ingredient from BHP.

item.title: Amazon nears Globalstar acquisition to challenge Starlink
item.description: Amazon is on the verge of acquiring satellite operator Globalstar in a deal that could be announced as early as Tuesday, according to Bloomberg News, marking a dramatic escalation in the tech giant's push to compete with SpaceX's Starlink in the low-Earth orbit internet market.

item.title: US Hormuz blockade could cost Iran $435 million a day
item.description:
The United States naval blockade of Iranian ports, which took effect on Monday at 10:00 a.m. Eastern Time, could inflict roughly $435 million in daily economic damage on Iran, according to an analysis first reported by The Wall Street Journal.

The estimate, compiled by Miad Maleki, a senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies and former official at the Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control, breaks down to approximately $276 million per day in lost exports — primarily crude oil and petrochemicals — and $159 million per day in disrupted imports. In a detailed thread on X, Maleki noted the figures assume Iran exports 1.5 million barrels of oil daily at a wartime price of about $87 per barrel, with more than 90 per cent of that volume shipping through Kharg Island in the Persian Gulf.

item.title: IEA says global oil demand will fall as Iran war boosts China's clean-tech exports
item.description:
The war in Iran has produced what the International Energy Agency calls the "largest supply disruption in the history of the global oil market" — and China, the world's dominant clean energy manufacturer, is emerging as a primary beneficiary.

Despite being Iran's largest oil customer, China is positioned to gain from the fossil fuel shock because it controls the supply chains the world now needs most. The nation accounts for more than 80 percent of global solar manufacturing, wind turbine production, and battery capacity, according to an analysis by Columbia University's Center on Global Energy Policy. As oil prices surged more than 60 percent in March alone, governments and households from Southeast Asia to Europe have accelerated their search for alternatives — and Chinese firms are ready to supply them.

item.title: Greenpeace warns of 'catastrophic' collapse risk at Chernobyl
item.description: Greenpeace Ukraine issued a stark warning on Monday that the internal radiation shell at the defunct Chernobyl nuclear power plant faces a growing risk of uncontrolled collapse, which could scatter highly radioactive material into the environment nearly 40 years after the world's worst nuclear disaster.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV pilgrimages to St. Augustine's ruins in Algeria
item.description: Pope Leo XIV traveled to the eastern Algerian city of Annaba on Tuesday, making a pilgrimage to the ancient ruins where St. Augustine — the fifth-century theologian who shaped Western Christianity — lived, preached, and died. The visit marks a spiritual homecoming for the first American-born pope, who has described himself as "a son of Saint Augustine."

item.title: US blockades Iranian ports as both sides eye fresh talks before ceasefire expires
item.description: The United States military began enforcing a blockade of all maritime traffic entering and leaving Iranian ports on Monday, a dramatic escalation even as Washington and Tehran explore a possible return to the negotiating table with one week remaining before a fragile ceasefire expires on April 21.

item.title: Israel, Lebanon hold first direct talks in decades
item.description: Israeli and Lebanese ambassadors are meeting in Washington on Tuesday for the first direct diplomatic talks between the two countries in over three decades, a session hosted by Secretary of State Marco Rubio at the State Department. The meeting, while historic in scope, faces deep divisions over its core objectives — with Israel demanding Hezbollah's disarmament and Lebanon pressing for an immediate ceasefire in a war that has killed more than 2,000 people since early March.

item.title: Xi warns of world 'crumbling into disarray' as Spain PM seeks China's help on Iran
item.description: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez met Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing on Tuesday, pressing China to use its diplomatic weight to help end the war between the United States and Israel against Iran and defuse the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz. Sánchez told Xi he could think of "few better interlocutors" than China to resolve the situation, according to The Diplomat in Spain, as the two leaders pledged to deepen ties and defend multilateralism against what Xi called a world "crumbling into disarray".

item.title: Von der Leyen calls for ending EU foreign policy vetoes after Orbán's defeat
item.description:
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen moved swiftly on Monday to capitalize on Viktor Orbán's stunning electoral defeat in Hungary, calling on EU member states to abandon the unanimity requirement in foreign policy and shift to qualified majority voting — a change that would strip any single country of the power to block decisions on sanctions and military aid.

Speaking at a press conference in Brussels, von der Leyen described the move as essential to prevent "systematic blockades" of the kind Hungary imposed during Orbán's 16-year rule, when Budapest repeatedly vetoed Ukraine aid packages and Russia sanctions. She hailed the victory of Péter Magyar and his center-right Tisza party as "a victory for fundamental freedoms," comparing it to Hungary's 1956 anti-Soviet uprising and its 1989 break from communism.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV presses on in Algeria after twin suicide bombings rock first day of visit
item.description: Pope Leo XIV arrived Tuesday in the Algerian city of Annaba to walk in the footsteps of St. Augustine, pressing ahead with his historic pilgrimage even as twin suicide bombings on the first day of his visit cast a shadow over the trip.

item.title: Italy suspends defense deal with Israel in reversal by Meloni
item.description:
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni announced on Tuesday that her government has suspended the automatic renewal of its defense cooperation agreement with Israel, a move that came just hours after the deal was set to extend for another five years.

"In view of the current situation, the government has decided to suspend the automatic renewal of the defense agreement with Israel," Meloni said on the sidelines of an event in Verona, according to Italian news agency ANSA.

item.title: Pakistan pushes for new U.S.-Iran talks as port blockade enters second day
item.description: The United States military began enforcing a blockade of all maritime traffic entering and exiting Iranian ports on Monday, escalating a six-week-old conflict as diplomatic efforts to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz have so far failed. Vice President JD Vance, who led marathon negotiations with Iran in Islamabad over the weekend, defended the move as a direct response to what he called Iranian "economic terrorism."

item.title: Ships slip past US blockade of Iran despite CENTCOM's zero-breach claim
item.description:
U.S. Central Command declared Tuesday that no ships successfully breached its naval blockade of Iranian ports during the first 24 hours of enforcement, even as independent maritime data suggested several vessels slipped through the Strait of Hormuz unchallenged.

CENTCOM said in a post on X that more than 10,000 U.S. Navy, Marine Corps, and Air Force personnel, over a dozen warships, and dozens of aircraft are deployed to enforce the blockade, which took effect at 1400 GMT on Monday. Six merchant vessels complied with orders to turn back toward Iranian ports in the Gulf of Oman, the command said. The blockade is being "enforced impartially against vessels of all nations entering or departing Iranian ports and coastal areas," CENTCOM stated, while emphasizing that freedom of navigation remains in place for ships transiting to non-Iranian ports.

item.title: Saudi Arabia urges US to lift Hormuz blockade as standoff enters second day
item.description: Saudi Arabia is pressing the United States to pull back its naval blockade of Iranian ports in the Strait of Hormuz, warning that the escalation risks destabilizing the region and triggering Iranian retaliation, according to India Today reporting on Monday. The diplomatic push comes as the U.S. military's blockade entered its second day on Tuesday, with Washington and Tehran locked in a standoff over the world's most important oil chokepoint.

item.title: Oil dips as Iran war fuels historic shift to renewables
item.description:
The war in Iran, now in its seventh week, has disrupted roughly 20 percent of the world's oil supply through the Strait of Hormuz and sent energy prices to levels not seen since 2022 — but it has also intensified a global pivot toward renewable power that analysts say could reshape energy markets for decades.

Oil prices dipped below $100 a barrel on Tuesday as Iran's president signaled willingness to end the conflict, according to The New York Times, but remained roughly $35 higher than a year ago. The crisis, triggered by U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran beginning February 28, led to the effective closure of the strait and strikes on at least 23 oil and gas sites across the region.

item.title: US, Iran eye new peace talks as Hormuz blockade enforcement falters
item.description:
The United States and Iran are in discussions for a second round of face-to-face negotiations after weekend talks in Islamabad ended without a deal, even as a U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports took effect Monday and tanker movements through the Strait of Hormuz tested both sides' resolve.

A White House representative confirmed Tuesday that negotiations are entering a "potential second phase," though no official timeline has been established, CNBC reported. Reuters reported that U.S. and Iranian teams could return to Islamabad as soon as Thursday, though the venue, timing, and delegation details remain undecided, with Geneva also under consideration. The ceasefire is set to expire next week, adding urgency to the diplomatic push.

item.title: New footage shows Artemis II capsule opening after Moon mission splashdown
item.description: Four days after splashing down in the Pacific Ocean, newly released footage is offering a closer look at the recovery of NASA's Artemis II crew following their 10-day journey around the Moon — the first crewed lunar mission in more than half a century.
